ui.1967: Admetia — master’s admissions, careers and moving for work
ui.1968: A free, independent reference for choosing a master’s, understanding careers, getting hired and moving country: 136 programmes, 154 role families and 46 countries, with every figure sourced. In English and Italian.
ui.1969: Where are you trying to get to?
ui.1970: Admetia is a free, independent reference for four decisions: which master’s to apply to, which career it leads to, how to get hired, and how to move country for it. Start from the question you have. Nothing here asks you to sign up or choose a profile first, and you can move between the parts at any time.
ui.1972: Compare 136 MBA, business and computing programmes by what each one requires, what it costs and when it closes. Then test your profile against each school’s published rules.
ui.1974: 154 role families in 13 fields: what the work is like, what it pays, how hard it is to get in, and which degrees lead there. Useful before deciding whether further study is worth it.
ui.1976: How people actually get hired in 46 countries, when each recruiting season opens, and how to prepare the CV, the letter and the interview. Separate routes for students, new graduates and people already working.

ui.1978: 46 countries and 200 city hubs: what each one hires for, the visa route on your passport, pay against rent, daily life, and what to do in the first weeks after you arrive.

ui.1986: You do not need to know the names of degrees or jobs to begin. Three ways to look around, none of them a commitment:
ui.1987: Answer 8 to 17 questions about what you studied, what you would enjoy doing and how you want to work. It ranks the role families against your answers and shows why. Optional, and you can skip it and browse instead.
ui.1989: Pick your degree subject and see which role families are a strong fit, a possible fit or a stretch, with the reason for each.
ui.1991: Open a country to see what its cities hire for, then follow the links to how hiring works there and which roles are involved.
ui.1992: What this is, and what it is not
ui.1993: An independent, unofficial reference built for personal use. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to any university, employer or government. Nothing on it is admissions, careers, legal or immigration advice: every figure is dated and sourced so that you can check it, and the pages say plainly where something could not be verified. How the information was gathered and checked.
ui.1995: Two ways in, and they work together. Look through every programme with what it requires, what it costs and when it closes; or answer a calculator’s questions and see where your profile stands at each school. If you are still deciding whether a master’s is the right step, start from the careers it leads to.

ui.2000: Seven calculators check each school’s hard rules first, then score your profile under that school’s own weighting. Your answers stay in this browser.
